mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate general partner by duly authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if executed outside Luxembourg

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, general partners, authorized managers and counterparties against the United Nations and European Union consolidated financial sanctions lists, the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance freezing list, and the Luxembourg domestic PEP register; OFAC SDN list screening is applied as an internationally accepted best practice given the use of USD Swift wire rails for crew payroll; enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any politically exposed person under the Law of 12 November 2004, and requires documented source-of-wealth analysis; ongoing transaction monitoring is required under CSSF Regulation 12-02; negative news screening is performed via LexisNexis, World-Check or an equivalent commercial database; results are archived in the AML/UBO file for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); online e-Registry at www.lbr.lu and MyGuichet.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The RCS accepts corporate names in any language expressed in the Latin alphabet; the statutory form designation must appear as 'Société en commandite spéciale' or the acronym 'SCSp' in French or another official language recognized by the RCS; non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Latin characters with a certified translation into French; ambiguous or misleading names are rejected on grounds of public order and market confusion.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: OPCVM / UCITS / Organisme de placement collectif
État / State / Gouvernement / Government / Commune / Municipality
Croix-Rouge / Red Cross / Institutions nationales ou internationales
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the LBR issues a reasoned refusal notice; the filer may within five (5) business days submit an amended name through the LBR e-Registry, or file a formal written objection to the RCS registrar within one (1) month of the refusal; an administrative appeal may then be brought before the Director of LBR, followed by judicial review before the Tribunal administratif de Luxembourg, with interim relief available by 'référé' if irreparable harm is demonstrated; final factual review lies with the Cour administrative; all judicial steps require a Luxembourg avocat and the accompaniment of the RCS refusal notice together with any prior ministerial authorization obtained for sensitive tokens.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable only through a Luxembourg regulated domiciliation agent under the Law of 31 May 1999; a pure mail-forwarding or virtual address without any operational substance is not acceptable for a crew recruitment agency processing multi-currency payroll; at minimum the SCSp must maintain a general partner with management authority in Luxembourg and, where payroll and crewing services are rendered, an engaged local manager, premises and employment records commensurate with the maritime staffing business.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of 30-40% for an unannounced on-site control within the first three years; the risk increases to approximately 55% if the SCSp processes crew payroll exceeding EUR 1.0 million per annum or claims Luxembourg substantive activities while relying purely on domiciliation; on-site inspections are executed by the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), the Luxembourg Maritime Administration and AML/CFT supervisory authorities.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), in particular the SCSp regime (Articles 124-1 et seq. inserted by the Law of 12 July 2013); read with the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and the amended Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 January 2003 on the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), attached to the Tribunal d'Arrondissement de Luxembourg, with electronic filing through the LBR/MyGuichet.lu portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: SCSp Partnership Agreement (contrat de société / acte de société sous seing privé) executed in writing, filed with the RCS and published in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital, no paid-up capital requirement, and no escrow account requirement under Luxembourg law for an SCSp; capital contributions are freely determined by the partners and recorded in the partnership agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [SCSp], dated [DATE], adopted in a session of the General Partner acting as managing organ. RESOLVED, that the contributions of the partners, as listed in the Partnership Agreement, are hereby approved and fully subscribed; the General Partner is instructed to file the deed with the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the SCSp is established at [address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, as stated in the deed. RESOLVED, that [NAME] is appointed Manager with sole signature authority to represent the SCSp, open bank accounts, and execute contracts. RESOLVED, that the Manager shall apply for the business establishment permit and the maritime crew recruitment licence, and comply with all regulatory obligations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of SCSp partnership agreement and partner qualification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Parties' legal counsel and, at the parties' option, any notary in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg (a private deed is sufficient; notarisation is not mandatory for an SCSp with an office-services object).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the SCSp deed in French (or bilingual English/French) recording the firm name, registered office, corporate object, capital contribution schedule, share formula, and the appointment of the sole General Partner. Each partner, or its duly authorised attorney-in-fact, must sign the deed. Corporate partners must attach board resolutions and certified registration extracts, and every general partner must confirm absence of personal bankruptcy or professional disqualification.
required_dossiers: Passport or ID copy of each natural-person partner
Certified corporate registration extract and authorising resolution of each corporate partner
Draft SCSp partnership agreement (statuts)
Registered office address proof or written consent of the premises owner/lessor
Declaration of no personal bankruptcy for each general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries the form or language of the deed, retain the private deed and file a sworn translation by a Luxembourg sworn translator; if signatures are challenged, obtain legalised signatures or execute a rectifying addendum before the original signatories.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration filing with Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) – Luxembourg Business Registers (lbr.lu), registry of the Tribunal d'Arrondissement de Luxembourg.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic filing through the LBR portal (or at the RCS counter) enclosing the signed partnership agreement, the standard identification form of the SCSp, and the manager's written acceptance; pay the prescribed registration fee. The registrar issues the registration receipt and the 13-digit national business number (matricule).
required_dossiers: Signed SCSp partnership agreement
RCS standard identification form (Formulaire B)
Written acceptance of the Manager/General Partner
Proof of registered office (ownership title, lease, or lessor consent)
Power of attorney and counsel ID if filed via a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a formal notice to complete deficiencies is issued, cure within the one-month statutory period by supplementary filing; a refusal may be challenged before the RCS controller and thereafter by court application to the Tribunal d'Arrondissement de Luxembourg.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the RESA electronic gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS / Luxembourg Business Registers, acting as registrar of the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request and verify publication of the statutory legal notice containing the SCSp's name, registered office, partners, capital contributions, and Manager. Publication is generally automated upon registration; the SCSp's counsel should retain the official RESA excerpt as proof of third-party effectiveness.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate of registration (extract)
Partners' and Manager's details for the legal notice
RESA notice text following the RCS template
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication notice is erroneous or incomplete, file a corrective notice and an application for rectification with the RCS within 15 days of discovery; re-publication fees are waived where the defect is attributable to the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and social security registration (NIF, VAT, corporate tax file, employer registration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the RCS certificate with the AEDT to obtain the Luxembourg VAT identification number and confirm the national business number; instruct the ACD to open the corporate income tax file; if the SCSp will run Luxembourg payroll for shore staff, register as an employer with the CCSS. The SCSp is fiscally transparent, but registration and filing obligations still apply.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate of registration (matricule)
SCSp partnership agreement
Identity documents of the Manager/General Partner
SCSp bank account details (opening confirmation or IBAN notice)
Employer registration questionnaire (for CCSS, if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax file is not opened automatically, apply directly via MyGuichet.lu or by registered letter to the AEDT/ACD; if the VAT number is not issued within 15 days, escalate to the competent tax office with a copy of the RCS certificate and a reminder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business establishment permit and seafarer crew recruitment licence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction de la Création d'Entreprises (via MyGuichet.lu); co-competent authority: Administration de la Marine Marchande (Luxembourg Maritime Administration) for the seafarer recruitment and placement service under the Maritime Labour Convention, 2006 (MLC 2006).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for the Autorisation d'établissement proving the Manager's good repute, professional capacity, and the absence of bankruptcy. For the MLC 2006 seafarer recruitment and placement component, submit a compliance dossier describing the crewing process, seafarer welfare safeguards, liability cover, and a written undertaking to supervise vessel crew recruitment in conformity with MLC 2006 Chapters 1 and 5.
required_dossiers: Application form for the Autorisation d'établissement
RCS extract of the SCSp
Certificate of good conduct (extrait du casier judiciaire) of the Manager
Evidence of professional liability insurance (minimum EUR 1,000,000)
MLC 2006 seafarer recruitment and placement conformity procedure
Organisational chart, crewing process description, and staff employment contracts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure deficiencies within the three-month objection window; any refusal may be appealed to the Minister of the Economy within 40 days of notification and thereafter to the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction de la Création d'Entreprises; Administration de la Marine Marchande (Luxembourg Maritime Administration) for maritime crew recruitment; Ministry of Labour for private employment agency oversight.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit under the Law of 2 September 2011) and MLC 2006 Seafarer Recruitment and Placement Licence/Recognition Certificate.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Environment Agency of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class 3 – Exempt from mandatory EIA: office-only crewing agency activity not listed in the annexes to the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment; no IPPC/Industrial Emissions Directive status and no environmental operating permit required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emission limits applicable; office waste is limited to municipal, paper, and WEEE streams handled under the Law of 21 March 2017 on waste management and the applicable municipal collection ordinances; if the office floor area exceeds 500 m², the Grand-Ducal Regulation on indoor environmental quality for tertiary buildings applies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety inspection and clearance by the Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours (CGDIS) covering alarm systems, extinguishers, and unobstructed egress; occupational clearance by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) for electrical installations (Grand-Ducal Regulation of 27 February 2019), first-aid equipment, ergonomic workstations, and emergency procedures; no structural-load modification is required for a standard office lease, but a structural load certificate is retained for landlord sign-off.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direct taxes: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), 33 boulevard Roosevelt, L-2015 Luxembourg (https://impotsdirects.public.lu). VAT, registration duties and estate taxes: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) (https://pfi.public.lu). Business registry and statutory identification: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) for RCS and RBE (https://www.lbr.lu). E-filing of VAT and related declarations: eCDF (electronic Customs and Fiscal Declarations) portal; general e-government services: MyGuichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An SCSp used as a ship crew recruitment agency must be incorporated and filed at the RCS through the LBR to obtain the national business identification number (numéro d'identification, 17-digit matricule) and complete the RBE beneficial-ownership registration. VAT registration is effected with the AEDT (via eCDF/MyGuichet) using VAT Forms 1 or 2 (for established and non-established persons respectively), resulting in a Luxembourg VAT identification number (N° TVA) within 2–4 weeks. Since the SCSp is fiscally transparent, it is not a direct-tax taxpayer itself, but it must file an annual informational declaration (déclaration de renseignements) with the ACD allocating income to general and limited partners. Each partner, including non-resident corporate partners, must obtain a Luxembourg taxpayer number (N° d'immatriculation) and file its own tax returns. Foreign entities conducting crew-management activity through a Luxembourg permanent establishment must register that PE with the ACD within one month of commencement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — The SCSp is fiscally transparent by statutory default under Article 2(1) of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (LIR). It is not subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) or net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune) at entity level; income, expenses and tax attributes pass through pro rata in accordance with the partnership agreement and are taxed at partner level. Resident partners are taxed on worldwide income; non-resident partners are taxed in Luxembourg only on Luxembourg-source income, including profits attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment. Crew recruitment income (ISIC 5222) is ordinary business income. No tax-exempt economic zone applies in Luxembourg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: (i) Opt-in to corporate tax treatment: under Article 2(2) LIR, as amended by the Law of 23 July 2016, an SCSp may elect, with the unanimous consent of all partners and subject to statutory conditions, to be treated as a capital company subject to CIT, municipal business tax and net wealth tax; the election is filed with the ACD and is binding for at least five fiscal years. (ii) Hybrid mismatch rules: Luxembourg applies EU ATAD 1/2 hybrid mismatch provisions (LIR Articles 168quinquies et seq.), relevant where a foreign jurisdiction classifies the SCSp as a separate taxable entity (e.g., via a US Form 8832 check-the-box election); the reverse-hybrid rule requires a Luxembourg transparent entity to be treated as opaque if formed in Luxembourg, controlled by a foreign partner, and the partnership income would otherwise be untaxed. (iii) VAT grouping: the SCSp and its Luxembourg fixed establishment(s) may form a VAT group (assujettis unis) with other Luxembourg VAT taxable persons. (iv) No general unilateral check-the-box election exists under Luxembourg domestic direct tax law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée under the Luxembourg VAT Code (Loi TVA of 12 February 1979), fully aligned with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC; no GST, sales tax or use tax regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 30,000 — small-business franchise exemption (Article 50 Loi TVA): a Luxembourg-established taxable person whose annual taxable turnover excluding VAT does not exceed EUR 30,000 may be exempt from VAT registration and invoicing obligations; registration is mandatory once the threshold is exceeded or when the business opts to register to recover input VAT. Non-established foreign suppliers of B2B crew services must apply Luxembourg reverse-charge and place-of-supply rules; registration is required where the place of supply is Luxembourg. The EU EUR 10,000 cross-border distance-sales threshold applies only to B2C supplies of goods and electronically supplied services. Reference rate note: the standard VAT headline rate increased from 17% to 18% with effect from 1 January 2025.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not impose real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, government API integration or digital stamping for B2B invoices. E-invoicing is permitted under EU standard EN 16931 (Peppol BIS 3.0 UBL); B2G e-invoicing for public procurement has been mandatory since 18 October 2020 for contracting authorities operating e-invoicing. B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary and paper or PDF invoices are generally valid. VAT returns, EU recapitulative statements (EC Sales Lists) and INTRASTAT declarations are filed electronically through the AEDT eCDF portal. No government approval of invoice data is required in real time. Luxembourg has committed to the EU ViDA reforms calling for mandatory e-invoicing and digital reporting for cross-border supplies by 2030, but the current regime remains an open e-invoicing framework.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% export VAT rate may be claimed under Article 44(1)(a) of the Loi TVA, implementing Article 148(1)(a) of EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC, which exempts with credit the supply of services for the direct needs of seagoing vessels used in maritime traffic (commercial, industrial, rescue or fishing operations) and their cargo. A ship crew recruitment and management agency (ISIC 5222) may zero-rate services such as crew placement, manning, payroll administration, and crew changeover/transport when the services are directly linked to a qualifying vessel. Eligibility conditions: (i) the vessel must be a seagoing vessel operating on the high seas for commercial, industrial, rescue or fishing purposes, not a pleasure craft; (ii) the service must be supplied at the request of and for the operational needs of the shipowner or operator; (iii) the supplier must obtain and retain contemporaneous evidence of vessel identity and use and of the direct-need link; and (iv) the service must not be a standalone headhunting or HR service disconnected from a specific vessel, which would be taxable at 18%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (ÉvD/MRN) and exit confirmation — required only for physical export of goods to non-EU destinations; not applicable to pure crew services
Bill of Lading or Vessel Manifest evidencing the vessel's international voyage and crew deployment
Inward Remittance Certificate — bank confirmation of fee repatriation from the foreign shipowner or paying agent
Crew management agreement with the shipowner/operator together with the vessel's IMO registration certificate confirming seagoing commercial use
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg has no statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline specific to export services; the 180-day benchmark aligns with the UCC 150-day exit-confirmation rule applied by analogy to goods and with the requirement that zero-rating evidence be available no later than the filing deadline of the periodic VAT return. The AEDT scrutinises export and zero-rating claims with elevated intensity, and the burden of proving vessel qualification and direct need rests on the taxpayer. If a claim is disallowed, the AEDT issues a corrective assessment restating standard-rate (18%) VAT, and the following sanctions may apply: (1) statutory late-payment interest of 0.8% per month (9.6% per annum); (2) administrative penalties up to 10% of the assessed VAT, increased to 20%–50% in cases of bad faith or deliberate concealment; (3) criminal prosecution for fraudulent zero-rating with fines up to EUR 125,000 or twice the tax evaded and imprisonment for responsible officers; (4) extension of the standard 5-year assessment period to 10 years in fraud cases, permitting retrospective clawback of input VAT credits and reclassification of exports; and (5) personal and joint liability of the SCSp's general partner for VAT penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking prudential supervision; BCL acts within the European System of Central Banks (ESCB) and applies ECB monetary and FX reporting frameworks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a Eurozone member with a fully liberalised capital account. Both current and capital account transactions are freely convertible for residents and non-residents, with no general exchange control restrictions. Profit remittance, liquidation proceeds, and investor distributions are freely transferable, subject only to anti-money-laundering (AML/KYC) due diligence, EU/UN sanctions screening, and standard tax formalities (including verification of the SCSp's tax transparency status and potential anti-abuse withholding rules under the ATAD and Luxembourg domestic law).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender obligation, mandatory conversion ratio, or forced repatriation timeline exists under Luxembourg law. Export and related service receipts may be retained in any currency. Reporting is required solely for Balance of Payments statistics under ECB Regulation (EU) No 2013/33 and BCL instructions; entities must file monthly or quarterly statistical returns when transaction thresholds are met, but no commercial restrictions or conversion obligations apply.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Crew Payroll and Multi-Currency Settlements)
Capital Escrow Account (Partnership Contributions and Investor Initial Deposits)
Operational Account (Trade Payments, Commercial Letters of Credit, and FX Hedging)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. EU-authorised Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) licensed under PSD2 and passporting into Luxembourg may be used as supplementary clearing rails for lower-risk crew payroll disbursements and seafarer money transfers. However, such EMIs cannot replace a Luxembourg licensed credit institution for receiving investor capital contributions, holding client funds in escrow, or executing structural corporate transactions. Offshore (non-EEA) digital EMIs are not viable due to CSSF supervisory expectations, European AML/CFT rules, and the absence of reliable EUR correspondent banking relationships for a Luxembourg-domiciled SCSp.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, Luxembourg banks require at least one physical in-person interview for the general partner of an SCSp or the account signatories for non-EU directors. Remote opening is permitted only for EU/EEA residents using eIDAS-compliant qualified electronic signatures and video identification recognised under CSSF guidelines. Non-EU directors must provide a notarised, apostilled identity package and usually need to appoint an authorised Luxembourg representative or domiciliation agent for compliance service and document service.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Layered SCSp ownership through non-EU limited partners causing ambiguous Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) identification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated UBO excerpt from the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), notarised partnership agreement, full organisational chart, copy of notarised and apostilled passports for every natural person owning more than 25%, and a Luxembourg legal opinion confirming the absence of bearer shares or nominee arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound capital injections from high-risk jurisdictions or trust structures without a transparent source-of-wealth trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital introduction letter stating non-refundable equity nature, six months of source-of-funds bank statements, sworn source-of-wealth declarations, tax clearance certificates from the investor's jurisdiction, notarised general partner resolution approving the capital call, and supporting precedent transaction documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to a dispersed maritime workforce in multiple jurisdictions, including payroll cards, cash-like disbursements, and third-party crew agents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master crew agreement, individual employment contracts, MLC 2006 compliant crew list, detailed payroll registers, seafarer identity documents, vessel manning agency agreements, exact SWIFT/SEPA payment instructions, per-pay-period audit trail, and the agency's annual AML internal review report.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All investor capital contributions must be routed via SWIFT MT103 (or equivalent DVP/FCY instruction) to the SCSp's main Luxembourg bank account. The remittance information (field 70/77B) must include the SCSp partnership reference, the definitive capital call notice number, and the investor's UBO code. Purpose codes should follow BCL Balance of Payments classification, typically 'S.2.2' for investment in the own capital of the partnership, with a matching OECD BPM6 code where applicable. Any contribution above the bank's internal threshold must be pre-cleared with the compliance office before execution to prevent AML flags.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For Euro-denominated crew payroll, SEPA Credit Transfers (SCT) are executed as the primary clearing rail, using the SCSp's Luxembourg IBAN and SWIFT interconnection. For non-EUR payments to non-SEPA jurisdictions, SWIFT MT103 wires via correspondent banks are used. For vessel supplies and larger operational procurements, commercial Letters of Credit (MT700) issued by the SCSp's bank in favour of the supplier provide settlement security. Multi-currency payroll can be aggregated and settled via virtual IBANs or dedicated currency sub-accounts to reduce FX conversion layers and ensure traceability.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD and EUR/GBP deliverable FX forward contracts (plain vanilla, maturity-matched to payroll cycles and trade payables) executed with a licensed Luxembourg or EU credit institution
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CIRS) for any SCSp financing or operating credit facilities, structured under ISDA/CSA agreements
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with limited convertibility in seafarer remittance corridors where physical EUR/USD settlement is impracticable
Vanilla FX options (puts and calls) used exclusively for risk management of crew payroll and charterer receivables, never for speculative exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: RCS Annual Data Confirmation (Déclaration Annuelle RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days of RCS annual e-notice; absent notice, on registration anniversary before 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing reminder fee of EUR 25; repeated failure triggers compulsory judicial liquidation or administrative strike-off from RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO Register Annual Confirmation (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 December, confirming beneficial ownership as at 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years for the responsible manager (Law of 13 January 2019); publication of non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Deposit (Dépôt des Comptes Annuels) — large SCSp only
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RCS for publication; Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) Central Balance Sheet Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after financial year-end; mandatory only if 2 of 3 size thresholds exceeded
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered compliance with fines to EUR 10,000; continued omission exposes the SCSp to RCS strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Establishment Authorization Annual Renewal (Renouvellement de l'autorisation d'établissement)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Direction générale des PME) via MyGuichet.lu; crew recruitment agrément overseen by Ministry of Mobility and Public Works
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 January; crew-staffing licence must be continuously valid
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Cease-and-desist order for unlicensed regulated activity; administrative penalties and licence revocation for persistent breach

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Partnership Annual Informational Tax Return (Déclaration fiscale SCSp)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 December of the succeeding tax year for online filers; paper filers earlier by official calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Assessment of penalties up to EUR 10,000 plus default interest; risk of estimated assessment against the general partner

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit required where the SCSp exceeds 2 of 3 thresholds: EUR 6.25M balance-sheet total, EUR 12.5M net turnover, 50 average employees (Law of 19 December 2020)
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: LUX GAAP per Luxembourg accounting law; IFRS permitted for statutory accounts of consolidated groups; payroll and vessel-crew receivables booked per ISIC 5222 maritime staffing activity

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Mandatory annual LBR confirmation by 31 December; ownership transfers additionally declared within 1 month per Law of 13 January 2019; SCSp is transparent so the general partner and any limited partner with >25% interest are presumptive UBOs

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Exempt below size thresholds; typically USD 13,000 — USD 48,000 when triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: SCSp is fiscally transparent; no CIT at partnership level. Luxembourg resident commercial companies are taxed at 17% CIT (above EUR 175,000) + 7% solidarity surcharge (1.19%) + municipal business tax (6.75% in Luxembourg City), yielding an aggregate headline rate of 24.94%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The SCSp benefits from full pass-through: partners enjoy double taxation treaty access, no capital gains tax on qualifying participations (80% participation exemption for corporate partners under certain conditions), and exemption from the 0.5% net wealth tax if held by a governing body qualifying as an investment fund. No statutory tax holidays apply to crewing agencies.
